status: Unaccepted finite dual-level chute challenger; no physical, capacity, escape or flood pass

low.scope: Sealed lower conduit carrying common collector flow; pressure, seals, vents, supports and outlet admission are unproved.

upper.scope: Open upper rain trough with horizontal side tops and 300-wide return into shaft; physical first-harm, hydraulic, seal and structural qualification open.

chuteCollars.scope: Three lower conduit collars are sealed around the wall penetration; upper return notches remain open to the shaft. Actual walls, structure and leak paths are unproved.

shaftReference.scope: Closed sided splash shaft under collector, central pitched canopy and open end discharge; structural/flow/weather admission absent.

states.normal: Common collector feeds closed lower conduits; exposed upper trough catches the directly intercepted adjacent roof drips. Both run towards their free ends outside deck edge.
states.endBlockage: A blocked lower conduit returns pressure to collector and thence shaft; a blocked upper end backs water to the +6320 notched return at y5350 into the shaft, provided that return and shaft are open. Each must be challenged with one whole-event stress; no actual capacity or physical flow test exists.
states.shaftBlocked: If the return/shaft itself is obstructed, rising water can overtop the upper +6382 side onto the deck. This common-mode state FAILS: no harmless ground spill or reliable worker retreat is demonstrated.

limits: The middle rail at y6150/+6190 passes through each tall side-wall envelope; sealed penetrations around the complete rail and structurally supported guard/cleaning access must be designed. The numerical section is not a fabricated guard.

Each 300-wide return, collector entrance, covered conduit, end spill, pressure cap, seals, support and side-wall junction must be detailed and challenged independently at full event. Actual losses, wind, splash, debris, ice, air and freeboard invalidate any automatic inference from ideal weir arithmetic.

The lower cap and sidewalls must resist water head and load; the upper surface must actually deliver direct roof water to its free end or return without leakage. Seal and structural ratings are not inferred.
Full common blockage or high site tailwater is not solved by an ideal clean return; the screen, ground splash, first harm, weathering, egress and independent rescue remain unqualified.
The raised body, selected hoist arm and connections remain geometric reservations rather than an actual product assembly.
